title: Recall Quiz: Edmund Spenser & The Faerie Queene

questions.q: Who referred to Edmund Spenser as 'the poet's poet'?
questions.explanation: Charles Lamb, the Romantic essayist, famously gave Spenser this title due to his massive influence on other poets.

questions.q: In Book I of The Faerie Queene, what virtue does the Redcrosse Knight represent?
questions.explanation: The Redcrosse Knight is the patron of Holiness.

questions.q: The Spenserian stanza consists of how many lines?
What is the rhyme scheme of the Spenserian stanza?
questions.explanation: The interlocking rhyme scheme is ababbcbcc.

questions.q: What is the specific metric name given to the final (ninth) line of a Spenserian stanza?
questions.explanation: The 9th line is an iambic hexameter, which is known as an Alexandrine.

questions.q: In The Faerie Queene, Britomart is a female knight representing the virtue of:
questions.explanation: Britomart represents Chastity in Book III.

questions.q: Which of Spenser's works is a collection of 12 pastoral poems, one for each month of the year?
questions.explanation: The Shepheardes Calender consists of 12 eclogues.

questions.q: Spenser's 'Amoretti' is a sequence of sonnets written to commemorate his courtship of:
questions.explanation: He wrote Amoretti and Epithalamion for his second wife, Elizabeth Boyle.
